title: Number systems cheat sheet
markdown:
A page to keep open while you read memory.

## One hex digit is four bits

| Hex | Binary | Decimal | | Hex | Binary | Decimal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0000 | 0 | | 8 | 1000 | 8 |
| 1 | 0001 | 1 | | 9 | 1001 | 9 |
| 2 | 0010 | 2 | | A | 1010 | 10 |
| 3 | 0011 | 3 | | B | 1011 | 11 |
| 4 | 0100 | 4 | | C | 1100 | 12 |
| 5 | 0101 | 5 | | D | 1101 | 13 |
| 6 | 0110 | 6 | | E | 1110 | 14 |
| 7 | 0111 | 7 | | F | 1111 | 15 |

## Powers of two

| Power | Decimal | Hex | Where you meet it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2⁴ | 16 | `0x10` | One hex digit's worth |
| 2⁷ | 128 | `0x80` | The top bit of a byte |
| 2⁸ | 256 | `0x100` | Values in one byte |
| 2¹⁰ | 1,024 | `0x400` | A kilobyte |
| 2¹² | 4,096 | `0x1000` | A page of memory |
| 2¹⁶ | 65,536 | `0x10000` | Values in two bytes |
| 2²⁰ | 1,048,576 | `0x100000` | A megabyte |
| 2³¹ | 2,147,483,648 | `0x80000000` | The top bit of a 32-bit value |
| 2³² | 4,294,967,296 | `0x100000000` | Values in four bytes |

## Type sizes on 64-bit Windows

| Type | Bytes | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `bool` | 1 | `false` or `true` |
| `char` | 1 | -128 to 127 |
| `unsigned char`, `std::uint8_t` | 1 | 0 to 255 |
| `short` | 2 | -32,768 to 32,767 |
| `unsigned short`, `std::uint16_t` | 2 | 0 to 65,535 |
| `int`, `long`, `std::int32_t` | 4 | about ±2.1 billion |
| `unsigned int`, `std::uint32_t` | 4 | 0 to about 4.29 billion |
| `long long`, `std::int64_t` | 8 | about ±9.2 quintillion |
| `float` | 4 | about 7 significant digits |
| `double` | 8 | about 15 significant digits |
| any pointer | 8 | an address |

## Values worth recognising

| Hex | Decimal | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | 0 | Zero, `false`, `nullptr`, the end of a C string |
| `0x0A` | 10 | The newline character |
| `0x20` | 32 | The space character |
| `0x30` to `0x39` | 48 to 57 | The characters `0` to `9` |
| `0x41` to `0x5A` | 65 to 90 | The characters `A` to `Z` |
| `0x61` to `0x7A` | 97 to 122 | The characters `a` to `z` |
| `0x7F` | 127 | Largest signed byte |
| `0x80` | 128 | Most negative signed byte, read as -128 |
| `0xFF` | 255 | A byte with every bit on, read as -1 when signed |
| `0x7FFFFFFF` | 2,147,483,647 | Largest `int` |
| `0xFFFFFFFF` | 4,294,967,295 | Largest `unsigned int`, read as -1 when signed |

## Reading multi-byte values in memory

PCs are little-endian: the lowest byte comes first.

| Bytes in memory | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `01 00 00 00` | `int` | 1 |
| `E8 03 00 00` | `int` | 1000 (`0x000003E8`) |
| `FF FF FF FF` | `int` | -1 |
| `2C 01` | `short` | 300 (`0x012C`) |
| `78 56 34 12` | `int` | `0x12345678` |

## In C++

```cpp
#include <format>
#include <iostream>

int main()
{
    int value{ 1000 };
    std::cout << std::format("{}  0x{:X}  0x{:08X}  {:#b}\n", value, value, value, value);
    std::cout << 0x3E8 << ' ' << 0b11'1110'1000 << '\n';
    return 0;
}
```
```
1000  0x3E8  0x000003E8  0b1111101000
1000 1000
```
